answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A single operator can still create many keys, but each key ties up capital, and slashing the bond for proven fraud makes mass Sybils expensive rather than merely tedious. The rule should apply equally to a falcon routing work across an ocean and to a bot at a wharf: identity counts only when backed by collateral at risk.
